newsitem.title: MEXICO: Zedillo says Mexico to maintain peso float in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Zedillo says Mexico to maintain peso float in 1997.

text.p: Mexico will maintain a free-floating peso in 1997, as well as fiscal and monetary discipline, because it would be "risky" to commit to a different exchange rate regime, President Ernesto Zedillo said on Friday.

"The economic strategy will involve...the maintenance of a exchange policy where the value of the currency continues to be determined by market forces," Zedillo told an annual meeting of industrialists.

"It would be incongruent and even risky to commit to an exchange rate policy according to a band of flotation or a pre-determined sliding rate," he said at the event, organized by the Confederation of Industrial Chambers (Concamin).
He said such exchange rate regimes would put, to a large extent, "the future economic fate of the country in the hands of speculators."
In the previous administration of ex-President Carlos Salinas, Mexico had exchange rate bands and a pre-determined, or crawling-peg, slide in the peso's value against the dollar.
Zedillo outlined his economic strategy for next year, that he said would remain based on strict fiscal and monetary discipline.

"Within the framework of this discipline we will absorb the cost of the reform of the social security system...and of the substantial financial support that we have had to channel to different sectors because of the 1995 crisis," he said.
Growth would be at least four percent, he said.
He also said policy would be aimed at promoting domestic savings to spur productive investment instead of financial speculation.

"The free float according to market forces will help determine the exchange rate congruent with the indispensible participation of the export sector...and congruent with economic growth," Zedillo said.
